definitions.explanation: Concentric circular waves spreading outward from a point of disturbance on a water surface.
The spreading impact or consequences of an event, especially something controversial or disruptive.

examples.japanese: {石|いし}を{投|な}げると{波紋|はもん}が{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: Ripples spread when I threw a stone.

examples.japanese: {水面|すいめん}に{美|うつく}しい{波紋|はもん}ができた。
examples.english: Beautiful ripples formed on the water's surface.

examples.japanese: {池|いけ}に{落|お}ちた{葉|は}が{小|ちい}さな{波紋|はもん}を{描|えが}いた。
examples.english: A leaf that fell into the pond traced small ripples.

examples.japanese: その{発言|はつげん}は{大|おお}きな{波紋|はもん}を{呼|よ}んだ。
examples.english: That remark caused a big stir.

examples.japanese: {辞任|じにん}のニュースが{政界|せいかい}に{波紋|はもん}を{広|ひろ}げた。
examples.english: The news of the resignation sent ripples through the political world.

examples.japanese: あの{事件|じけん}が{社会|しゃかい}に{投|な}げかけた{波紋|はもん}は{今|いま}も{消|き}えていない。
examples.english: The repercussions that incident cast over society have still not faded.

notes:
WRITING:
{波|は} (wave) + {紋|もん} (pattern). Literally "wave pattern."

USAGE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is extremely common in news and formal writing, often in the set phrase {波紋|はもん}を{呼|よ}ぶ (to cause a stir/repercussions) or {波紋|はもん}を{広|ひろ}げる (to spread repercussions).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波紋|はもん}を{呼|よ}ぶ: to cause a stir
- {波紋|はもん}を{広|ひろ}げる: to spread ripples/repercussions
- {波紋|はもん}が{広|ひろ}がる: ripples/repercussions spread
- {波紋|はもん}を{投|な}げかける: to cause ripple effects
